response.reason: Candidate 0 (2810–2812): Verified on detail plot; a narrow downward dip (~0.15 z-units, 3 pts) interrupts a flat plateau phase where normal cycles show zero roughness and no micro-wiggles (ref 0, 3). This violates piecewise-constancy and is distinct from accepted micro-wiggles (≥4 pts, ≤0.2 amp). Boundary tight and correct; confidence remains high (0.94). Candidate 1 (4125–4129): Detail plot shows a symmetric upward spike (~2 pts wide, Δy≈+0.04), but reference normals never exhibit upward impulses—even micro-wiggles are downward and low-magnitude. However, the amplitude is extremely small (<0.05 z-units) and could be quantization noise; more critically, the surrounding signal is clean staircase with no morphological disruption, and the event does not match any known anomaly pattern (point anomalies require globally extreme values; this is not extreme). Downgraded to rejected. Candidate 2 (2400–2415): Visible range [2272,2543] shows the descent starts at 2400, but the preceding plateau is absent—yet the next plateau begins at ~2416, confirming the abnormal descent spans 2400–2415. Reference cycles always have a sharp 1–2 pt step after a plateau; here the descent is gradual over 15 pts, violating morphology. Confirmed as shapelet; confidence 0.82 upheld. Candidate 3 (2947–2952): Detail plot shows 6-point zigzag (3–4 alternations, ~0.25 amp), exceeding normal micro-wiggle specs (≤2 pts, ≤0.2 amp). No similar pattern elsewhere; not raster artifact (consistent across zoom). Verified as shapelet; confidence 0.82 upheld. Candidate 4 (2855–2856): The claimed single-point drop of −0.20 is misread: on the detail plot (2727–2984), the ramp ends at index 2855 (value ≈−4.98), then at 2856 it drops to ≈−5.05 (Δy≈−0.07), matching normal step magnitude (e.g., 2829–2830: −4.92→−4.99). The steepness is illusory due to y-axis scaling; no violation exists. Rejected as false positive.
